text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - The CCC bought 8,000 tonnes U.S. soft red winter wheat for donation to Jamaica. The wheat was bought from Cargill at $175.83 a tonne for October 5-30 delivery.

- The CCC bought 23,194 tonnes U.S. wheat for donation to Honduras. It bought 4,750 tonnes of NS/DNS wheat from Peavey Co at $181.84 a tonne and 2,844 tonnes of soft red winter wheat from Peavey at $176.69 for Nov 1-25. The deal includes 9,600 tonnes of NS/DNS wheat from Peavey at $181.84 and 6,000 tonnes SRW wheat from ADM at $174.87, set for Dec 10-30.

WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd and Cheiljedang Corp on Friday bought a total of 21,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Japanese trading firm Marubeni Corp, traders in Seoul said. Cheiljedang bought 9,000 tonnes at various prices, basis March futures on the Chicago Board of Trade, traders said. Shipment was set for January 1-31 from the Pacific Northwest to the southeastern ports of Pusan and Ulsan, they said.
RICE SALE - Jordan bought 18,803 tonnes U.S. medium grain rice under the PL 480, Title I export program for Nov 15-30 delivery, its U.S. export agent and U.S. exporters said.

RICE SALE - Ivory Coast bought 26,516 tonnes U.S. no.2 long grain brown rice under PL 480 program. The first shipment of 18,000 tonnes was for Oct 15-Nov 15 and included 6,000 tonnes at $355.24 a tonne and 6,000 tonnes at $359.89 from Louis Dreyfus, plus 6,000 tonnes from Connell Rice at $362.99. Another 8,516 tonnes was for Nov 15-Dec 15 from Dreyfus, with 6,000 tonnes at $356.74 and 2,516 tonnes at $363.39 a tonne.

CORN SALE - Taiwan Sugar Corp bought a 10,000-tonne No.2 or better U.S. yellow corn from Marubeni Corp. The shipment was C and F at 89.75 U.S. cents a tonne over December Chicago futures. The shipment was for Dec 10-31 or Jan 1-20.
VEGOIL SALE - India's State Trading Corporation bought one parcel of palm olein for at $582 a tonne c and f for October 5-20 shipment, European vegetable oil traders said.

WHEAT TENDER - The Egyptian state's main grain buyer said on Friday he wanted bids for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red or soft wheat wheat on Saturday. The wheat is for loading between October 15 and 31. The result is due on Sunday.
- Egypt's official commodities buyer said he was extending the deadline to buy 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat until Sunday, September 15, to attract cheaper prices.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Dae Han Flour Mills Co Ltd said it passed on tenders for 12,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat due to high prices. Shipment was for January 15 to February 15 to the western port of Inchon.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 50,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale, a spokesman said. An international call had been issued, setting September 17 as the final date to receive price offers. Confirmation would be made on September 18. The amount would be ready for shipment from Oct 15 to Nov 14.
WHEAT TENDERS - Syria separately offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 was final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
- The CCC seeks 25,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the export donation program for Bosnia. Shipment is set for Oct 5-31 and bids are due on September 17.
- The CCC seeks up to 4,410 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Senegal. Shipment period is set for October 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.
- The CCC seeks 45,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, maximum moisture 13.5 percent to donation for Ethiopia. Shipment set for November 1-25 and offers due by Sept 19.
CORN TENDER - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.
- The CCC seeks up to 4,280 tonnes of U.S. No.2 yellow corn under the export donation program to Angola. Shipment period is slated for Oct 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.

MARKET TALK - Far Eastern grain traders said on Friday China recently bought 700,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat, bringing Beijing's total purchases from Canada for the current marketing year to 1.5 million tonnes.
